title: Event lane condensation for high-density time-series + tactile/ARIA pacing cues
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Problem: Our time-series charts can become visually and programmatically noisy when many discrete events (alerts, deployments, annotations) are displayed densely along the x-axis. Screen readers announce long lists of event labels; rendering many DOM markers increases layout cost and spikes CPU/GPU usage. Designers need a single, repeatable pattern that preserves discoverability and meaning while reducing DOM/paint overhead and improving perception for keyboard and mobile users.

Goal: Introduce an "event lane" condensation pattern plus accessibility pacing signals so: 1) high-density event series are grouped into semantic lanes and condensed glyphs (with a visual summary and count), 2) screen readers get concise, sequential summaries with an option to expand to detail, and 3) mobile receives optional haptic beats for temporal significance. The solution must be themeable via design tokens, use GPU-friendly rendering fallbacks, and be implementable with minimal runtime overhead in the serving runtime's telemetry charts and the Redwood Console.

Proposed solution overview: 
- Condensed event lanes: Group events into contiguous time buckets per lane (e.g., deployments, errors, releases). Each bucket renders a single condensed glyph (striped dot, mini-band) plus a numeric badge when counts exceed threshold. Lanes collapse visually at small widths into summary rows. 
- Progressive reveal: Hover/focus/open will expand a bucket into a transient overlay showing individual event rows. This expansion is canvas-backed for performance; DOM is only created when expanded. 
- Accessible pacing cues: Introduce an ARIA "lane-summary" live region announcing the condensed summary as the user pans/zooms. For keyboard navigation, add step-by-step lane navigation (NextLane/PrevLane) and an inline "read more" that focuses the expanded list. For mobile, add optional haptic pulses for critical buckets (configurable token).
- Token surface: New tokens for lane spacing, condensed glyph color ramp, badge scale, live-region verbosity, and haptic intensity label. Tokens documented in design system and mapped to CSS variables and mobile SDK tokens. 
- Rendering & perf: Default rendering uses a GPU-accelerated canvas layer with a light DOM overlay for badges and interactive handles. For low-power or accessibility-first mode, fallback to semantic DOM lists but with virtualization. Batching and compositing strategies will be documented for eng.

Tradeoffs considered: 
- Haptics: Great for mobile signal, but adds platform divergence. We propose haptics off by default and opt-in via chart options. 
- Canvas vs DOM: Canvas is faster for dense glyphs but reduces direct accessibility for individual events. We mitigate via live-region summaries and on-demand DOM expansion. 
- Summarization granularity: Too coarse loses actionable detail; too fine retains clutter. We'll default to 30s buckets for high-density telemetry charts with user-overrides.

Acceptance criteria (must be satisfied before Done): 
1) Design spec with tokens, states, microinteractions, and visual examples for desktop/tablet/mobile. 
2) Accessibility spec: ARIA roles, live-region copy, keyboard flows, and SR regression checklist. 
3) Engineering handoff package: components, expected data shape, interaction contract, and canvas/DOM hybrid notes. 
4) Perf target: rendering of 10k events downsampled to condensed lanes should not add more than 5% frame drop on mid-range machine compared to current baseline. 
5) Usability validation: 5 user sessions with keyboard-only and screen reader; adjustments documented.

Deliverables: design spec Figma file, token mapping docs (CSS variable + mobile token names), annotated prototypes (desktop and mobile), accessibility checklist, and a short demo recording for demo day.
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff workshop completed with Eng (Aisha, Paolo) and PM (Diego). Scoped lanes: deployments, alerts, annotations. Agreed buckets are application-configurable.
2026-02-27: First mockups added to Figma. Explored three condensed glyphs: pill, mini-band, and striped-dot. Team prefers mini-band for legibility in dense views.

2026-03-03: Accessibility review w/ Lea (a11y). Key feedback: live-region copy must avoid noisy repeated announcements; provide a quiet summary + explicit expand command. Also suggested keyboard shortcuts for lane navigation.
2026-03-05: Performance sync with runtime team. Decided on canvas-first rendering with on-demand DOM hydration. Eng requested explicit APIs for 'expand bucket' to avoid full DOM creation during pan.
2026-03-08: PM asked to add mobile haptics as opt-in. Design added haptic intensity token and a mobile toggle in chart settings mockup.
2026-03-10: Prototype V1 ready for internal playtest. Preparing engineering handoff and acceptance criteria checklist. Scheduled SR review on 2026-03-18.
